zh-CN.title: 道可道，非常道
zh-CN.shortSummary: 《道德经》开篇以语言、命名与恒常之间的张力建立阅读问题。
curatorialDescription: 段落不被处理成拒绝语言的口号，而与版本、章次和后续注释一起展示。
zh-CN.researchNote: Alpha 暂据通行本，需补出土本异文和唐代注本。

quote.original: 道可道，非常道；名可名，非常名。

interpretation.zh-CN: 可说、可名与恒常之间的张力是本章的起点。
interpretation.en: The chapter opens with a tension between what can be spoken or named and what is constant.

en.title: A Dao that can be spoken
en.shortSummary: The opening of the Daodejing frames a problem among language, naming and constancy.
curatorialDescription: The passage is not reduced to an anti-language slogan; it is shown with edition, chapter and commentarial context.
en.researchNote: The Alpha text follows a received edition; excavated variants and Tang commentaries remain to be added.

quote.original: 道可道，非常道；名可名，非常名。

interpretation.zh-CN: 可说、可名与恒常之间的张力是本章的起点。
interpretation.en: The chapter opens with a tension between what can be spoken or named and what is constant.

profile.originalText: 道可道，非常道；名可名，非常名。
profile.punctuatedText: 道可道，非常道；名可名，非常名。
profile.modernZh: 能够说出的道，不是恒常的道；能够命名的名，不是恒常的名。
profile.translationEn: A Dao that can be spoken is not the constant Dao; a name that can be named is not the constant name.

zh-CN.title: 上善若水
zh-CN.shortSummary: 水的比喻把利物、不争与处下联系起来，是一组关系性描述。
curatorialDescription: 页面保留完整句群，避免只截取四字格言。
zh-CN.researchNote: 需补版本异文与主要注本对“善”“不争”“处下”的解释。

en.title: Highest goodness is like water
en.shortSummary: The water metaphor connects benefiting things, non-contention and dwelling in low places as relational qualities.
curatorialDescription: The full sentence group is retained instead of extracting a four-character maxim.
en.researchNote: Variants and major commentaries on goodness, non-contention and low position remain to be added.

profile.originalText: 上善若水。水善利万物而不争，处众人之所恶，故几于道。
profile.punctuatedText: 上善若水。水善利万物而不争，处众人之所恶，故几于道。
profile.modernZh: 最高的善像水：滋养万物而不争，处在众人不愿处的位置，所以接近于道。
profile.translationEn: Highest goodness is like water. Water benefits all things without contention and dwells where people dislike; thus it is close to the Dao.

zh-CN.title: 为学日益，为道日损
zh-CN.shortSummary: 章句以“益”与“损”对照学习积累和趋向无为的实践方向。
curatorialDescription: “损”不被简单译成反知识，而需在整章和注释传统中理解。
zh-CN.researchNote: 需补通行本异文、注本和英译比较。

en.title: In learning one increases; in the Dao one decreases
en.shortSummary: The passage contrasts accumulation in learning with a practice of decreasing toward non-forcing.
curatorialDescription: Decrease is not rendered simply as opposition to knowledge; it must be read within the chapter and commentarial traditions.
en.researchNote: Received variants, commentaries and translation comparison remain to be added.

profile.originalText: 为学日益，为道日损。损之又损，以至于无为。无为而无不为。
profile.punctuatedText: 为学日益，为道日损。损之又损，以至于无为。无为而无不为。
profile.modernZh: 求学每日增加，行道每日减损；减损又减损，直到无为，而无为并非无所成就。
profile.translationEn: In learning one increases daily; in the Dao one decreases daily, decreasing until non-forcing, through which nothing is left undone.

zh-CN.title: 学而时习之
zh-CN.shortSummary: 《论语》开篇把学习、按时践习与愉悦联系起来。
curatorialDescription: “习”同时保留复习、实践与养成的解释空间，不固定为单一现代学习法。
zh-CN.researchNote: 需补古注、唐代经学注疏和英译差异。

en.title: To learn and practise at due times
en.shortSummary: The Analects opens by connecting learning, repeated practice and pleasure.
curatorialDescription: Xi retains space for review, enactment and habituation rather than becoming one modern study technique.
en.researchNote: Early commentary, Tang classical exegesis and translation variants remain to be added.

profile.modernZh: 学习并按时温习和践行，不也是令人愉悦的吗？
profile.translationEn: To learn and practise at due times—is this not a pleasure?

zh-CN.title: 三人行，必有我师焉
zh-CN.shortSummary: 章句把学习置于与他人同行、辨别优点并反省自身的关系中。
curatorialDescription: 完整句群同时包含效法与自我修正，不只是一句赞美谦逊的格言。
zh-CN.researchNote: 篇章编号、古注和唐代解释需进一步核对。

en.title: When three walk together, there is surely a teacher for me
en.shortSummary: The saying places learning in companionship, discernment of strengths and self-correction.
curatorialDescription: The full passage includes both emulation and correction, not only a maxim about humility.
en.researchNote: Chapter numbering, early commentary and Tang interpretation require further verification.

profile.originalText: 三人行，必有我师焉。择其善者而从之，其不善者而改之。
profile.punctuatedText: 三人行，必有我师焉。择其善者而从之，其不善者而改之。
profile.modernZh: 多人同行，其中一定有可作为我老师的人；选择其优点学习，见到不足则反省并改正自己。
profile.translationEn: When three walk together, there is surely a teacher for me: I follow what is good in them and correct in myself what is not.

zh-CN.title: 己所不欲，勿施于人
zh-CN.shortSummary: 这句回答把“恕”表达为从自身不愿承受之事出发约束对待他人的方式。
curatorialDescription: 段落保留问答和德目语境，不把它脱离关系伦理改写为孤立口号。
zh-CN.researchNote: 需补《卫灵公》篇语境、古注和唐代注疏。

en.title: Do not impose on others what you do not desire
en.shortSummary: The answer expresses shu as restraint in treating others, beginning from what one would not wish to bear oneself.
curatorialDescription: The passage remains in its question-and-virtue context rather than becoming an isolated slogan detached from relational ethics.
en.researchNote: The Wei Ling Gong context, early commentary and Tang exegesis remain to be added.

profile.modernZh: 自己不愿承受的事情，不要加在别人身上。
profile.translationEn: Do not impose on others what you do not desire for yourself.
